| Subcommand | Runs |
|---|---|
| `dk` (no argument) | The full TUI |
| `dk setup` | A standalone context-creation wizard — see [Run the setup wizard](../how-to/run-the-setup-wizard.md) |

There is no flag-parsing framework behind this — `setup` is a single literal
match on `os.Args[1]`, and it's the one thing that has to run *before* any
context is loaded, since it's what creates the first one.

content.text:
## Verification report — `dk setup` documentation

**Source files:** `main.go`, `internal/ui/setup/{model.go,wizard.go,commands.go,answers.go,fields.go}`, `internal/config/config.go`

### Claim 1 — "runs standalone, no context loaded first, works before `~/.devdesk/` exists"
**VERIFIED.** `main.go:38-44` dispatches on `os.Args[1] == "setup"` and calls `setup.Run()` *before* `config.Load()` / `config.EnsureConfigDir()`, which only happen in `runTUI()` (`main.go:55-65`). The setup package doc comment (`model.go:1-6`) states the same.

### Claim 2 — Six ordered steps as described
**VERIFIED**, with one nuance. Step constants (`model.go:23-36`) are declared in exactly this order: `stepFontCheck, stepContextName, stepSecretBackend, stepContainerEngine, stepTheme, stepForgeType, stepForgeURL, stepForgeNamespace, stepForgeVisibility, stepForgeCloneMethod, stepForgeToken`. The doc's "Forge" (item 6) bundles the last 6 internal steps into one topic — content-accurate, but the wizard's own footer literally counts `stepCount = 11` (`fields.go:43`, `"Step %d of %d"`), so a user doing forge config sees e.g. "Step 9 of 11", not "step 6 of 6". Worth a docs tweak but not a factual error.
- Font-check copy matches "before anything else risks looking broken" in spirit (`fields.go:137-142` comment: "a broken font is caught before the user spends the rest of setup looking at boxes and question marks").
- Secret backend "checks live whether reachable": `commands.go:73-78` (`checkSecretBackendCmd` → `credentials.Select`).
- Container engine "checks live... daemon actually answers, not just PATH": `commands.go:91-106` + comment explicitly makes this distinction; `checkContainerEngineCmd` calls `engine.Resolve` then `docker.FetchCapacity()`.
- Theme "fetched from the DevDesk repository": `answers.go:119-131`, `remoteThemeBaseURL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthnel/devdesk/main/themes/"`.
- Forge token "validated live against the real API before it's saved": `commands.go:49-62`, `session.NewAuth(...).Authenticate(...)`.

### Claim 2b — Context name charset "lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, or `default`"
**VERIFIED exactly.** `internal/config/config.go:878-896`: `ValidateContextName` special-cases `"default"`, else regex `^[a-z0-9-]+$`.

### Claim 3 — "Every field except context name can be left blank... wizard still creates the context either way"
**VERIFIED for text fields, imprecise for cycle fields.** `fields.go:100-105` (URL: "Leave it blank to skip forge configuration"), `:108-113` (namespace: "Leave it blank if you don't have one"), `:127-132` (token: "Leave it blank... DevDesk will still create the context"). `advance()` (`model.go:305-324`) applies no validation except on `stepContextName`. However, secret backend / container engine / theme / forge type / visibility / clone method are closed-set cycle fields (Rule 132) that always carry a selected default — they have no "blank" state to leave; the doc's wording glosses over this distinction but doesn't misstate behavior (nothing blocks proceeding with the default).

### Claim 4 — `←`/`→` cycle, `Enter` confirms/advances, `Esc` back-or-quit-from-first
**VERIFIED exactly.** `model.go:275-289` (`handleKeyMsg`): `"esc"→stepBack`, `"left"→cycle(-1)`, `"right"→cycle(1)`, `"enter"→advance`. `stepBack` (`model.go:294-301`): `if m.step == stepFontCheck { return m, tea.Quit }`, confirming Esc quits only from the first step.

### Claim 5 — Calls `config.SaveContext`, "identical to configuring by hand"
**VERIFIED.** `commands.go:113-117`: `saveContextCmd` returns `ContextSavedMsg{Err: config.SaveContext(cfg, name)}` — exact function name.

### Claim 6 — Asks before overwriting an existing context
**VERIFIED.** `model.go:467-482` (`handleContextExists`): if `msg.Exists`, shows a `confirmPrompt` "Context exists... will be overwritten. Continue?" before proceeding.

### Claim 7 — "Reports the path it wrote and any warning... then `dk` starts the full TUI against the context you just created"
**Reporting half: VERIFIED.** `fields.go:243-264` (`renderDone`): `"Wrote " + m.savedPath`, then `currentContextWarning` and `tokenSaveWarning` if set.

**"Then `dk` starts the full TUI": CONTRADICTED.** There is no chaining into the TUI anywhere:
- `main.go:38-44`: after `setup.Run()` returns (success or not), the branch `return`s — `runTUI()` is never reached.
- `wizard.go:5-11`: `Run()` only runs the wizard's own `tea.Program` and returns its error; no `app.New`/`tea.NewProgram` for the main app anywhere in `internal/ui/setup` (confirmed via grep — zero hits).
- The done screen itself tells the user to do this manually: `fields.go:259` — `` b.WriteString(`Run "dk" to start.`) `` — and `fields.go:261` — `` helpStyle.Render("  [enter] exit") ``. `model.go:268-273` confirms `enter`/`esc`/`q` on `stageDone` all just `tea.Quit`.

So `dk setup` exits the process after writing the context; the user must invoke `dk` again separately. The doc's final sentence should read something like "then exits — run `dk` to start the TUI against the context you just created."

### commands.md claim — `os.Args[1]` literal match, runs before context load
**VERIFIED.** `main.go:38`: `if len(os.Args) > 1 && os.Args[1] == "setup"`, and the comment at `main.go:34-36` states essentially the same rationale as the docs line.

---

**Summary:** Every claim checks out against the code except the closing sentence of the how-to doc — "then `dk` starts the full TUI against the context you just created" is factually wrong; the process exits and the user must run `dk` again. That's the one fix needed before merging. The "six ordered steps" framing is a defensible simplification of an internal 11-step counter, and "every field... can be left blank" slightly overgeneralizes from text fields to cycle fields, but neither rises to a contradiction.
